entries.title: The heat equation
entries.summaryHtml: A rod with its ends held at zero and a half-sine of heat along it. Diffusion damps a mode sin(mπx) at the rate κ(mπ)2, so the exact solution is u(x,t)=e−κπ2tsin(πx) — one number to get right, at every point.

entries.title: The heat equation in two dimensions
entries.summaryHtml: In two dimensions an implicit step couples every point to its four neighbors, and the matrix is no longer tridiagonal. Peaceman and Rachford's way around it: split the step in half, and be implicit in one direction at a time.

entries.title: The Black-Scholes equation
entries.summaryHtml: The price V(S,t) of an option on a stock at price S. It is a heat equation run backward from a known final condition — at expiry T a call is worth its payoff, max(S−K,0) — with diffusion 21​σ2S2 that grows with S, a drift, and a decay at the interest rate. Counting time to expiry, τ=T−t, turns it into an ordinary forward march.

entries.title: The advection equation
entries.summaryHtml: The simplest wave equation: whatever shape you start with slides along at speed c, unchanged. On a ring of length 1 it is back where it began after a time 1/c, which makes the exact answer the initial condition itself.

entries.title: The wave equation
entries.summaryHtml: A string fixed at both ends, plucked into its fundamental: u=sin(πx)cos(πct). Centered differences in both variables give the leapfrog scheme, un+1=2un−un−1+ν2(ui+1​−2ui​+ui−1​), with ν=cΔt/Δx.

entries.title: Burgers' equation with a shock and a rarefaction
entries.summaryHtml: Take the viscosity away and smooth data stops being enough: characteristics cross, the derivative blows up in finite time, and the solution continues as a shock. A finite difference of a discontinuity means nothing, so the method has to be built on the integral form instead — what flows into a cell minus what flows out.

entries.title: The Euler equations of gas dynamics
entries.summaryHtml: Mass, momentum and energy of a compressible gas, with p=(γ−1)(E−21​ρu2). Sod's problem is a membrane at x=21​ with dense, high-pressure gas on the left; at t=0 it bursts. Three waves come out: a rarefaction fan moving left, a contact discontinuity (density jumps, pressure and velocity do not) and a shock, both moving right.

entries.title: The time-dependent Schrödinger equation
entries.summaryHtml: Two operators, each trivial in its own basis. The potential multiplies ψ(x) by a phase; the kinetic energy multiplies ψ^​(k) by a phase. Neither can be applied exactly to the other's representation — but an FFT moves between them, so alternate: half a potential step, a full kinetic step, half a potential step. That is Strang splitting. Every factor is a pure phase, so the norm is conserved to rounding whatever the time step, and the error is O(Δt2), from the two operators failing to commute.

entries.title: The Korteweg-de Vries equation
entries.summaryHtml: Shallow-water waves, and the equation solitons were discovered in. Nonlinearity steepens a hump; third-order dispersion spreads it; and for exactly one family of shapes the two cancel: u=2c​sech2(2c​​(x−ct−x0​)). Taller solitons are narrower and faster — the speed c is twice the height.

entries.title: The nonlinear Schrödinger equation
entries.summaryHtml: Light in a fiber, a Bose-Einstein condensate, deep-water wave envelopes. Dispersion spreads a pulse; the focusing nonlinearity squeezes it. When they balance the pulse is a soliton, and the simplest is ψ=sech(x)eit/2: a shape that does not change at all, with a phase that turns at a steady rate.

entries.title: Burgers' equation, viscous
entries.summaryHtml: The smallest equation with both of a fluid's habits in it: uux​ steepens a wave, and νuxx​ smooths it. Where they balance the wave stops changing shape and simply travels: u=c−atanh(2νa(x−ct−x0​)​), a smoothed step from c+a down to c−a, of width about 4ν/a, moving at the mean of the two states.

entries.title: The Fisher-KPP equation
entries.summaryHtml: A population that grows logistically and spreads by diffusion: a gene through a species, a flame, an invading plant. Behind the front u=1, ahead of it u=0, and the front advances at a constant speed.
